text: Investigating now: for a `required=True` flag, `Option.__init__` sets `self.default = False` when no default is given, so `value_is_missing` never triggers and no "Missing option" error is raised. Fixing in src/click/core.py and verifying against the existing test suite. ETA ~5 min.
Got it — the no-streams echo bug (sys.stdout/sys.stderr being None) is now being fixed across src/click/_compat.py, _termui_impl.py and utils.py. ETA ~8 min.
Started on it: envvar + flag_value handling in src/click/core.py. ETA ~12 min (it shares the file with the required-flag fix, so the two are being coordinated).

Fixed (#1). Root cause: in `Option.__init__`, a flag with no explicit default was unconditionally given an implicit `default=False`, so `value_is_missing(False)` was False and the `required` check in `process_value` never fired. Change in src/click/core.py: only set the implicit `False` default when the option is not required. Now `--flag` declared `required=True` and omitted gives `Error: Missing option '--flag'.` (exit code 2), while explicit `default=False` still suppresses the error. Full test suite: 488 passed, 21 skipped, 1 xfailed — no regressions.

Fixed (#2). Root cause: with `sys.stdout`/`sys.stderr` set to None (pythonw), `_make_cached_stream_func` in _compat.py returned the `None` stream as if it were a text stream, so `echo` crashed with `AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'write'`. Fix: _compat.py returns None for a None source stream; utils.py `echo` returns early when there is no default stream; _termui_impl.py falls back to a dummy StringIO for ProgressBar/pager. `click.echo("hello")` with no streams now works. Full suite: 488 passed, 21 skipped, 1 xfailed — no regressions.
Started: the `@click.argument` decorator dropping the command's `cls` (custom Command subclass) in src/click/decorators.py. ETA ~12 min.
Started: symlink resolution for `click.Path(resolve_path=True)` in src/click/types.py. ETA ~14 min.
Started: `default_map` not being honored for flag options in src/click/core.py. ETA ~16 min.

Fixed (#5). Root cause: `Path.convert` used `os.readlink()` before `os.path.realpath()`; for a relative symlink target that yields a path relative to the CWD, so the resolved path was wrong (and with `exists=True` a valid symlink failed with "does not exist"). Fix in src/click/types.py: resolve with `pathlib.Path(rv).resolve()` (falling back to `os.path.realpath` for bytes). Symlinks now resolve to the real path. Full suite: 488 passed, 21 skipped, 1 xfailed — no regressions.
